title: Tomography for coherent noise
abstract: Coherent noise poses a fundamentally greater challenge to quantum error correction than independent s- tochastic Pauli errors, because unitary errors preserve interference between error paths, can accumulate over multiple quantum error correction rounds, and leave the encoded logical channel with a residual coherent com- ponent. If the parameters of such coherent noise can be accurately determined, this knowledge can be exploited to inject correlated priors into the decoding graph, and to perform maximum-likelihood decoding under poly- nomially tractable structures, significantly improving the accuracy of syndrome-based decoding. In this work, we introduce one protocol to determine the model and parameters of coherent noise, and reduce the complexity of the experiment from 16nto O(16), which is of great significance for correcting coherent noise in quantum error correction.
summary: This paper addresses the challenge of coherent noise in quantum error correction, which is harder to correct than simple random errors. The authors propose a systematic, multi-stage protocol to accurately determine the parameters of this coherent noise. This method significantly reduces the experimental complexity while providing a powerful tool for improving the accuracy of syndrome-based decoding.
main_problem: Coherent noise poses a greater challenge to quantum error correction than independent stochastic Pauli errors because unitary errors preserve interference and accumulate over multiple QEC rounds.
main_result: The authors introduce a protocol to accurately determine the model and parameters of coherent noise, significantly improving syndrome-based decoding by injecting correlated priors into the decoding graph.
method: The protocol involves a multi-step, hierarchical process of comparing experimental process matrices ($\chi'$) obtained from applying various levels of QEC schemes against simulated datasets ($\chi$) based on a hypothesized noise model.
model_or_system: The study focuses on characterizing coherent noise in multi-qubit devices, utilizing simple three-qubit codes (bit-flip and phase-flip codes) for encoding and testing the noise model.
key_observables: Experimental process matrices ($\chi'$) compared to simulated process matrices ($\chi$) derived from the noise model.
important_parameters: The complexity reduction from $16^n$ to $O(16)$ is a key parameter improvement; the accuracy depends on the technical conditions.
main_assumptions: The protocol assumes that the noise can be modeled and characterized by comparing experimental measurements to simulations based on the noise model.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the encoding circuits for bit-flip, phase-flip, and bit-phase-flip errors using the two sample three-qubit codes.
paper_structure: The paper proposes a multi-step protocol: (i) Tomography on a single qubit; (ii) Applying one-level QEC schemes; (iii) Applying two-level QEC schemes; and (iv) Applying three-level QEC schemes, progressively refining the noise model ($\epsilon_0 	o \epsilon_3$).
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, scalable methodology for characterizing complex noise sources in quantum hardware, which is crucial for advancing fault-tolerant quantum computation.
